newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat harvest ends, yields down in north.
newsitem.headline: French wheat harvest ends, yields down in north.

text.p: The French wheat harvest is complete after dry and hot weather allowed farmers in the north to make the last cuts over the weekend, local grain officials said on Tuesday.
In France's second soft wheat region of Picardie, ONIC officials confirmed yields would be 10 percent below last year's record levels of nine tonnes per hectare.
In the Nord-Pas de Calais, wheat yields were expected to decline to 8.0-8.5 tonnes from a a record 10 tonnes in 1996.
Despite a rise in area the soft wheat crop was expected to fall by 10 percent to some 4.1 million tonnes in Picardie, officials said.
Substantial rain in June and July, however, drove down test weight to very low levels of 73-74 kg compared to a standard 76 kg required by most buyers.
But protein content was satisfactory at 11-11.5 percent and there were few reports of germination.
Hagberg numbers of above 220 would also make the wheat fit for milling.
The region's barley harvest was also over and in the Picardie area officials confirmed forecasts of slightly lower yields of 7.6 tonnes per hectare against 7.8 or 7.9 tonnes in 1996.
But higher area would provide for a slight rise in barley output to some 900,000 tonnes, they said.
Barley quality was good in most areas, with the exception of the Somme, where the amount of small grain might make some crops unfit for malting.
